title: Do LLMs have core beliefs?
abstract: arXiv:2605.03255v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) has sparked debate about whether these systems exhibit human-level cognition. In this debate, little attention has been paid to a structural component of human cognition: core beliefs, truths that provide a foundation around which we can build a worldview. These commitments usually resist debunking, as abandoning them would represent a fundamental shift in how we see reality. In this paper, we ask whether LLMs hold anything akin to core commitments. Using a probing framework we call Adversarial Dialogue Trees (ADTs) over five domains (science, history, geography, biology, and mathematics), we find that most LLMs fail to maintain a stable worldview. Though some recent models showed improved stability, they still eventually failed to maintain key commitments under conversational pressure. translated_title: 大语言模型拥有核心信念吗？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）的兴起引发了关于这些系统是否具备人类水平认知的争论。在这场争论中，人类认知的一个结构性组成部分却很少受到关注：核心信念，即为我们构建世界观提供基础的真实信条。这些信念通常能够抵御驳斥，因为放弃它们将意味着我们看待现实的方式发生根本性转变。在本文中，我们探究大语言模型是否持有类似核心信念的东西。我们使用一个名为“对抗对话树”的探测框架，在五个领域（科学、历史、地理、生物学和数学）上进行测试，发现大多数大语言模型无法维持稳定的世界观。尽管一些最新的模型表现出了更好的稳定性，但在对话压力下它们最终仍无法维持关键的信念承诺。这些结果记录了模型各代际之间论证能力的提升，但表明所有（模型都）……
tldr: 本文提出“对抗对话树”探测框架，在五个知识领域测试发现大多数大语言模型无法在对抗性对话压力下维持稳定的世界观和核心信念，表明它们并不具备类似人类的核心信念。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Adversarial Dialogue Trees (ADTs), a probing framework across five domains, finding that most LLMs fail to maintain stable worldviews or uphold key commitments under conversational pressure, suggesting they lack human-like core beliefs.
